transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-04-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maria Gonzalez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Brightline Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Brightline CTO), Jasmine Park (Brightline Lead ML), Aaron Patel (Brightline Procurement)

Summary (auto):
- Renewal discussion for current hosted contract + request to expand to Dedicated capacity and add APAC region for low-latency retail features.
- Pricing addendum and 12-month extension proposed.
- Technical bench to validate latency and throughput; Redwood to provide capacity guidance and docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maria (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call, we got Liam, Priya, Jasmine, Aaron on Brightline and Ethan and I from Redwood. Sound good?
[00:10] Liam (Brightline): Yep, hi all.
[00:12] Priya (Brightline): Hi, thanks Maria.
[00:15] Maria: Great. The goal today is a renewal and expansion check-in — hear how Q2 usage is trending, talk Dedicated capacity for holiday season, and the APAC region ask you raised last week. We'll also cover next steps for procurement.
[00:30] Aaron (Brightline): Yep that's right. Procurement wanted the high level up front before we dig into numbers.
[00:35] Ethan (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll start with a quick run through of what Dedicated looks like for you, then we can get into capacity. Sorry, my mic is slightly echoey, bear with me.
[00:45] 
[02:10] Ethan: So Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, you get predictable throughput and isolation, we support configurable autoscaling and burst. For Brightline we looked at your Q4 traffic spikes last year — we recommend a mix of A100-equivalent instances for peak and some T4-style for background batch jobs. That yields a lower per-token cost and keeps p99 latency in check.
[02:40] Jasmine (Brightline): When you say A100-equivalent, are you referring to the NVidia — I think you mean A100 80GB or similar? We have some constraints in the APAC region though.
[02:50] Ethan: Yeah, A100 80GB class or comparable. In APAC availability varies by cloud provider; we can run a regional capacity plan. Redwood Dedicate — sorry, Redwood Dedicated — can spin up pools across regions but we need to decide on data residency and KMS for keys.
[03:10] Priya: Data residency is critical, we can't replicate EU/US PII into APAC without controls. Do you support customer-managed KMS in APAC?
[03:20] Maria: Yes, we do. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can integrate with a customer KMS in most regions — we'll confirm specifics for APAC in the docs we send.
[03:35] Aaron: Procurement needs SOC2 and also a note on audit logs retention for 12 months — is that standard?
[03:42] Maria: SOC2 Type II cert is available, we also have configurable audit log retention in the Console — default is 365 days for enterprise plans. We'll attach the SOC2 PDF to the follow-up.
[04:00] 
[06:05] Liam: On capacity side, our forecast for Q3 shows ~1.5x current token volume due to new personalized search feature. We want to avoid throttling during promotions. What buffer should we buy?
[06:20] Ethan: Given 1.5x, we'd recommend reserved capacity at 1.5x baseline plus 20% burst headroom for promotions. That means a temporary scale policy to cover 2x for short windows. We can model that and give you a cost delta.
[06:40] Jasmine: For the bench runs, can we pin a model version? We need to verify quality regressions when you suggested the quantized variant last quarter.
[06:50] Ethan: Absolutely. We support pinning model versions per route and can do a canary rollout. For the bench we'll spin up both float and quantized variants and measure latency and per-token cost, plus output diffs on a representative prompt set.
[07:05] Priya: That sounds good. Also are we able to route by region? We need requests from APAC to stay in APAC for latency and compliance reasons.
[07:15] Maria: Yes routing policies can be region-based. We can set default region = APAC for users in that locale and failover to US for dev/testing. There are also fallbacks to cheaper variants in an outage.
[07:28] 
[09:10] Aaron: On the contract, procurement is okay with a 12-month extension but we need clarity on exit terms and committed spend. Can you draft language for a 12-month term with an option to scale up?
[09:22] Maria: We can. Typical approach: committed monthly vCPU/GPU or committed $ amount with an overage rate. For Dedicated we do reserved capacity commits and allow burst usage billed at a discounted overage rate. We'll draft a clean addendum for you.
[09:40] Aaron: Great. Also need pricing that separates Hosted vs Dedicated line items for approval.
[09:46] Maria: Noted. We'll provide a pricing addendum link — pricing addendum link: https://redwood.example/pricing/brightline 
[10:00] 
[12:00] Liam: Performance: Our SREs saw p95 latency on current hosted endpoint at ~180ms in US, but APAC is 420-520ms which is too high for live checkout personalization. If we move to Dedicated in APAC what p95 can we expect?
[12:20] Ethan: If we provision region-local Dedicated with optimized kernels and the same model size you use now, p95 should drop into ~120-160ms depending on sequence length and batching. We'll validate with the bench and include request/response size breakdowns.
[12:40] Jasmine: Sequence lengths for checkout prompts average 80 tokens, but we do a lot of short prompts too. Also we rely on prefix caching (KV cache) heavily—how does KV cache work across regions?
[12:55] Ethan: KV cache is per-pool and per-tenant. For cross-region users we can populate cache locally or replicate warm prefixes to APAC; there's tradeoff on consistency and cost. We can discuss a hybrid approach in the bench.
[13:10] 
[15:30] Priya: Security — we need SSO with Okta and RBAC so product teams only access prod routes. Also IP allowlist for management plane.
[15:42] Maria: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and role-based access control in Console. IP allowlist for control plane and support for customer VPC peering. We'll attach configuration guides.
[16:00] Priya: And encryption in transit and at rest?
[16:05] Ethan: TLS in transit, and KMS for at-rest. For Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS or on-prem HSM if you choose Private.
[16:18] 
[19:00] Jasmine: For the bench, we'd like to run the test with our A/B test prompts and measure quality delta between float32 and int8 quantized. Any known issues with hallucination differences when quantized?
[19:12] Ethan: Generally small quality delta but depends on model and prompt patterns; our Optimize team has heuristics and a quantization profile per model to reduce regressions. We'll capture eval metrics and cadence so you can compare.
[19:30] Jasmine: Perfect. We'll share a 200-prompt set after this call.
[19:35] 
[25:00] Maria: Quick recap — Redwood to send pricing addendum and SOC2 + APAC notes, SE to run capacity estimate and schedule bench, Brightline to share prompts and forecast. Any other blockers?
[25:12] Liam: One small ask — can you provide a draft of the SLA for Dedicated latency targets?
[25:20] Maria: Yes, we'll include SLA language in the addendum. For Dedicated we can offer p99 latency targets with credit clauses; we'll propose specific numbers after bench results.
[25:32] Aaron: Procurement needs a single point of contact for invoicing and contract questions. Maria, that'll be you?
[25:38] Maria: Yes, I'll coordinate with you and loop in finance.
[25:42] 
[30:00] Ethan: Technical note — for the bench we'll likely run 3 configs: Hosted baseline, Dedicated float, Dedicated quantized. We'll mirror traffic shape for peak hour and run for 2-4 hours to catch autoscale behavior.
[30:18] Jasmine: Do you need our traffic replay or can Redwood synthetic?
[30:22] Ethan: Best is to replay your traffic for fidelity; we can augment with synthetic for edge cases. We'll provide instructions for log format.
[30:35] 
[36:00] Priya: Timeline question — we need APAC in time for the October campaign. Is that feasible?
[36:10] Maria: It's feasible; typical lead time for region rollout with Dedicated is ~8-12 weeks including procurement and capacity provisioning. If we start now and lock commits in April, October looks good. We'll include a deployment timeline in the follow-up.
[36:28] Liam: That's promising.
[36:35] 
[42:00] Aaron: Any concerns about vendor lock-in? Finance wants an ability to exit after trial window if quality or cost doesn't meet objectives.
[42:10] Maria: We can include milestone-based review points — 90-day bench/poC with success criteria defined and an option to renegotiate or exit if objectives not met. We'll put that in the draft.
[42:25] Priya: Good. Also a note for legal — data processing addendum and cross-border transfer clauses are needed.
[42:32] Maria: We'll attach DPA + standard SCCs where applicable.
[42:40] 
[48:00] Maria: Ok final recap of action items — Ethan will run capacity estimate and propose GPU mix; I'll send pricing addendum, SOC2, SLA draft and region notes; Brightline to share prompts and forecast. We aiming to have docs by next week.
[48:20] Aaron: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[48:25] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[48:27] Liam: Bye.

End of call.
